quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: The best protection when riding is:

options.text: Keep space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Distance is your best protection against hitting other vehicles. Keep plenty of space so you have time to react to other drivers' mistakes. Wearing proper gear is also important.

questions.question: The front brake provides how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?
questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: A person with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______ or higher is legally intoxicated.
questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: For people age 21 and older, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. Driving any vehicle while intoxicated is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: When riding at night, maintain a minimum following distance of:
questions.correctAnswerText: Three seconds
questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to see and judge distances. Keep at least three seconds of space behind the vehicle ahead. You need extra time to notice when it stops and to brake safely.

questions.question: Maximum braking in a straight line is accomplished by:

options.text: Using the rear brake while downshifting

questions.correctAnswerText: Using both brakes
questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes fully without locking either wheel for maximum stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: A linked braking system:

options.text: Connects the front and rear brakes so both apply when either lever is used
Connects the front brake to the gear shifter
Connects the rear brake to a foot control
Connects the rear brake to a switch on the handlebar

questions.correctAnswerText: Connects the front and rear brakes so both apply when either lever is used
questions.explanation: A linked braking system connects the front and rear brakes. When you use either brake lever, both brakes get pressure. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: Which vest or jacket color helps you be seen best?
questions.correctAnswerText: Red
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors while riding to be more visible. Bright orange, yellow, red, or green work best. Avoid dark or dull colors.

questions.question: When loading cargo on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Pack heavier items in front of the tank bag
Pack lighter items near the front
Avoid placing items over the rear axle
Place items behind the rear axle

questions.correctAnswerText: Pack heavier items in front of the tank bag
questions.explanation: Place heavier items in front of the tank bag. Load should go over or in front of the rear axle. Putting weight behind the rear axle can affect control.

questions.question: The center of a traffic lane is where:

options.text: Debris and oil from cars often collect

questions.correctAnswerText: Debris and oil from cars often collect
questions.explanation: The center of a lane collects debris and oil drippings from vehicles. Utility hole covers and other hazards also appear in the center of lanes.

questions.question: It is most important to flash your brake light when:

options.text: There is a stop sign ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: You will slow down suddenly
questions.explanation: A motorcycle has only one brake light, which is less noticeable than a car's two brake lights. Flash your brake light when braking suddenly so other drivers notice it.

questions.question: When riding in fog, you should:

options.text: Switch between low and high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlight.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in fog. High beams reflect off the fog and make it harder to see. Do not use high beams around other vehicles.

questions.question: How many paths of travel does each traffic lane give a motorcycle rider?
questions.correctAnswerText: Three
questions.explanation: Each lane has three paths: left, center, and right. Motorcycle riders can use any of these positions.

questions.question: When being passed, why should you not move to the far side of your lane?

options.text: It stops the passing driver from moving back early.
It may cause the passing driver to move back into your lane too soon.
It makes the passing driver complete the pass faster.
It encourages other drivers to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may cause the passing driver to move back into your lane too soon.
questions.explanation: Moving far to the side of your lane is dangerous. It may make the passing driver think there is room to return early. Stay in the center of your lane when being passed.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle rider?

options.text: The left side of the lane
The right side of the lane
The best position depends on your riding conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The best position depends on your riding conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is best for all situations. Choose your position based on road and traffic conditions. This helps you stay safe and be visible to other drivers.

questions.question: For passengers, a helmet:

options.text: Is required for those under age 18.
Is required only if the rider does not have a two-year license.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is required for those under age 18.
questions.explanation: Riders and passengers under 18 must wear approved helmets. Anyone on a motorcycle permit must also wear a helmet. All riders should wear helmets every time they ride.

questions.question: When riding in a lane of traffic, a motorcycle operator should:

options.text: Always ride in the same part of the lane.
Change lane position based on riding conditions.
Always ride in the center of the lane.
Always ride on the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lane position based on riding conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: A helmet should not:

options.text: Have been worn in a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have been worn in a crash.
questions.explanation: A good helmet must meet U.S. DOT standards, fit snugly, and have no visible damage. Never reuse a helmet after a crash. Replace it instead.

questions.question: When traveling in a group, riders should:

options.text: Spread out to be easier to see.
Stay close together to be easier to see.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay close together to be easier to see.
questions.explanation: Keep the group close but with enough space around each rider to move safely. This makes the group easier to see and keeps riders from getting separated. Do not pair up because riders need room to maneuver.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When you can see through vehicles ahead.
When weather is clear and pleasant.

questions.correctAnswerText: When traffic is heavy.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when heavy traffic, poor weather, wet roads, or nighttime conditions mean you need more space to stop. A two-second distance is normal for good conditions.

questions.question: Why should motorcycle riders not rely only on mirrors?

options.text: Motorcycle mirrors are smaller than car mirrors.
Motorcycles have blind spots like all vehicles.
Mirrors take your eyes off the road and should not be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots like all vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like cars do. Mirrors alone cannot show everything around you. Look over your shoulder frequently to check your blind spots.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of riding in a close group?

options.text: It uses less space on the highway.
The group is easy to see.
The group is less likely to get separated.
Riders reach their destination faster in a close group than in a spread-out group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders reach their destination faster in a close group than in a spread-out group.
questions.explanation: Riding in a close group is better than riding spread out because the group takes up less road space, is easier to see, and is less likely to separate at traffic lights and during passes.

questions.question: When riding in curves, turning, or entering a highway, the best group formation is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file.
questions.explanation: Staggered formation is usually best for group riding. However, riders should move into single-file when going through curves, making turns, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black lettering or symbols. All riders must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: A passenger should never:
questions.correctAnswerText: Ride sidesaddle.
questions.explanation: In South Carolina, passengers under 21 must wear a helmet and eye protection. All riders should wear helmets and eye protection. Passengers should not wear loose clothing that could catch on the motorcycle. Passengers must lean with the operator when turning. Passengers must never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: A motorcyclist can discourage other vehicles from lane sharing by:

options.text: Riding in the left portion of a lane.
Riding in the center portion of a lane.
Giving dirty looks if another driver moves into their lane.
Riding in a zigzag pattern to fill up a lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in the center portion of a lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to discourage other drivers from trying to squeeze into your lane.

questions.question: A proper lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Communicate your intentions to other road users.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you avoid traffic signals.
questions.explanation: A good lane position should help you see others and be seen. It should help you avoid wind blasts, other drivers' blind spots, and surface hazards. Your lane position should discourage lane sharing and give you an escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking alcohol and wants to drive, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Encourage friends to talk them out of driving.
Tell them to take less-crowded roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell them to take less-crowded roads.
questions.explanation: To prevent someone from driving while drunk, you can arrange other transportation, involve them in other activities to slow their drinking, use excuses to keep them from leaving before they are sober, and get other friends to help.

questions.question: When following a car, the best portion of the lane to ride in is usually:
questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane behind a car so you appear in the driver's rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors, so this position helps you be seen.

questions.question: When exiting a highway while riding in a group, which formation should be used?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file
questions.explanation: Staggered formation is usually best for group riding. Switch to single-file when going through curves, making turns, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.
questions.correctAnswerText: Seldom
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riders will rarely hear a tire going flat. Tire failure is usually noticed by how the motorcycle handles.

questions.question: You may need less space between you and the car ahead if:

options.text: You cannot see around the vehicle ahead.
The weather is good and traffic is light.

questions.correctAnswerText: The weather is good and traffic is light.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space between you and the car ahead when conditions are poor. Increase your distance if the road is slippery, you cannot see around the car ahead, or traffic is heavy.

questions.question: Studies show that most motorcycle crash riders:

options.text: Use the front brake too little and the rear brake too much.
Use the front brake too much and the rear brake too little.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front brake too little and the rear brake too much.
questions.explanation: Most riders in crashes use the front brake too little and the rear brake too much.

questions.question: When it starts to rain while you are riding, you should:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull to the edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane has oil that makes it slippery when wet. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars when it rains. Also slow down on wet roads.

questions.question: Where should you place a load on a motorcycle?

options.text: On one side of the motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible
questions.explanation: Keep loads low and secure them or put them in saddlebags. Do not stack loads high on the back, as this raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and affects balance. Distribute loads equally on both sides.

questions.question: When riding through a curve, you should:

options.text: Stay in the same part of the lane throughout the curve.
Always stay on the left side of the lane.
Always stay on the right side of the lane.
Know that the best path may not follow the road's curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know that the best path may not follow the road's curve.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change. Be ready to move to a different part of the lane at any time. The best path through a curve does not always match the curve of the road.

questions.question: When loading a motorcycle:

options.text: Put heavier items toward the front.
Put heavier items toward the rear.
Mount loads behind the rear axle.
Store lighter items in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put heavier items toward the front.
questions.explanation: Place heavier items toward the front of the load. Loads should be over or in front of the rear axle. Put lighter items behind you.

questions.question: The safest way to cross angled railroad tracks is to:

options.text: Go straight ahead in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go straight ahead in your lane.
questions.explanation: The safest way is to go straight in your lane when crossing angled railroad tracks. Turning to cross at a right angle is dangerous because it may push you into another lane.

questions.question: Which idea should NOT be used when planning a long group ride?

options.text: Plan travel segments based on the least experienced rider.
Skip breaks to reach your destination faster.
Place inexperienced riders behind the leaders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Skip breaks to reach your destination faster.
questions.explanation: Plan travel based on the least experienced rider's skill level. Take regular breaks to reduce fatigue. Place inexperienced riders behind the leader so experienced riders can watch them. Ride in a staggered formation.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks up, you should:

options.text: Keep holding the brake until the skid stops.
Release the front brake and do not use it again.
Release the front brake and then quickly squeeze it again.
Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks, immediately release the front brake completely. Then apply the brake smoothly.

questions.question: The front brake provides about how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?
questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.
